dhpak2.8:1.1: The English story title aligns with the Pāli title. The romanized editorial label Aññatarabhikkhussa Vatthu was removed because it has no separate corresponding Pāli passage.
dhpak2.8:3.4: visesetvā kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathāpessāmī means the bhikkhu intends to ask for his meditation subject to be explained further, not for a different subject ‘better suited to my needs.’
dhpak2.8:4.2: vegena says the bhikkhu climbed the bare mountain quickly; this action had been omitted from the English. The editorial heading ‘On Top of a Mountain’ was removed because it has no separate Pāli passage.
dhpak2.8:4.4: upādānāni are the fuel consumed by the forest fire. The English had called both this fuel and the fetters ‘obstacles.’
dhpak2.8:4.5: saṃyojanāni are fetters that the monk burns with the fire of noble-path knowledge; the English had called them ‘attachments.’
dhpak2.8:5.5: The Teacher says the fetters (saṃyojanāni) are to be burned with knowledge; the English had called them ‘attachments.’
dhpak2.8:5.6: obhāsaṃ vissajjetvā says the Teacher sent forth radiance and appeared as though sitting before the bhikkhu; the English had turned the radiance into ‘a radiant image of himself.’
dhpak2.8:6.1: The repeated Pāli transcription of verse 31 was removed because it has no separate corresponding passage in the local Pāli story.
dhpak2.8:6.2: ḍahaṃ says the bhikkhu advances while burning the fetter; the English had reduced this to advancing ‘against’ it.
dhpak2.8:7.1: The complete Pāli explanation of verse 31 has no English translation and remains Pāli-only under this paragraph.
dhpak2.8:8.2: sabbasaṃyojanāni says he burns all the fetters; the English ending had not preserved this detail.
dhpak2.8:8.5: vandamānova pakkāmi means the bhikkhu departed while paying homage, rather than after completing his homage.
dhpak2.8:9.1: The Pāli closing title Aññatarabhikkhuvatthu aṭṭhamaṃ is Pāli-only and has no English key.
